questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Paragraph: The grouping or assemblage of plants, animals and microbes we observe when we study a natural forest, a grassland, a pond, a coral reef or some other undisturbed area, is referred to as the area's biota or biotic community. The plant portion of the biotic community includes all vegetation, from large trees down through to microscopic algae. Likewise, the animal portion includes everything from large mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians through to earthworms, tiny insects and mites. Microbes encompass a large array of microscopic bacteria, fungi and protozoans. Thus, the biotic community comprises a plant community, an animal community and a microbial community. The particular kind of biotic community found in a given area is, in large part, determined by abiotic factors such as the amount of water or moisture present, the temperature, the salinity, or the type of soil in the areThese abiotic factors both support and limit the particular community. For example, a relative lack of available moisture prevents the growth of most species of plants, but supports certain species, such as cacti; these kinds of areas are deserts. Land with plenty of available moisture and a suitable temperature supports forests. The presence of water is the major factor that sustains aquatic communities. The first step in investigating a biotic community may be simply to catalogue all the species present. Species are the different kinds of plants, animals and microbes in the community. A given species includes all those individuals which have a strong similarity in appearance to one another and which are distinct in appearance from other such groups. Each species in a biotic community is represented by a certain population - that is, by a certain number of individuals that make up the interbreeding, reproducing group.
Question: Which one of the following does not belong to the biotic community?
questions.solution: Water is an abiotic component that supports biotic communities but is not part of the biotic community itself. The biotic community consists of living organisms like humans, protozoa, and bushes (plants).

questions.q: An infinite combination of resistors, each having resistance $R=4 \Omega$, is given below. What is the net resistance between the points A and B ? (Each resistance is of equal value, $R=4$ )
questions.solution:
Equivalent Resistance,
$\begin{array}{r}
y=\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{R} \| y \\
\Rightarrow y=\mathrm{R}+\frac{\mathrm{R} \times y}{\mathrm{R}+y} \\
\Rightarrow y=\frac{\mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{R} y+\mathrm{R} y}{\mathrm{R}+y} \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{R} y+y^2=\mathrm{R}^2+2 \mathrm{R} y \\
\Rightarrow y^2-4 y-16=0 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}} \text { or } y=2+2 \sqrt{5} \text { ohm }
\end{array}$

questions.q: A spherical shell of outer radius $R$ and inner radius $\mathrm{R} / 2$ contains a solid sphere of radius $\mathrm{R} / 2$ (see figure). The density of the material of the solid sphere is $\rho$ and that of the shell is $\rho / 2$. What is the average mass density of the larger sphere thus formed?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Average density }=\frac{\text { Total mass }}{\text { Total volume }} \\
& =\frac{\rho_1 V_1+\rho_2 V_2}{V} \\
& =\frac{\rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}\right)^3+\frac{\rho}{2}\left[\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3-\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}\right)^3\right]}{\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3} \\
& =\frac{\rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi \frac{\mathrm{R}^3}{8}+\frac{\rho}{2}\left[\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3-\frac{4}{3} \pi \frac{\mathrm{R}^3}{8}\right]}{\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3} \\
& =\frac{\rho}{8}+\frac{\rho}{2}\left[1-\frac{1}{8}\right] \\
& =\frac{\rho}{8}+\frac{\rho}{2}\left[\frac{7}{8}\right] \\
& =\frac{\rho}{8}+\frac{7 \rho}{16} \\
& =\frac{2 \rho+7 \rho}{16}=\frac{9 \rho}{16} .
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding animal cell membrane is correct?
options: They are composed of phospholipids only.
They are composed of proteins only.
They are composed of phospholipids and proteins only.
They are composed of phospholipids, proteins and cholesterol (lipid).
questions.solution: The cell membrane of animal cells is primarily composed of phospholipids, which form a bilayer structure. Embedded within or attached to this phospholipid bilayer are proteins that serve various functions like transport and signaling. Additionally, cholesterol molecules are interspersed among the phospholipids, contributing to the membrane's stability and fluidity. This composition of phospholipids, proteins, and cholesterol allows the cell membrane to regulate the passage of molecules and ions, maintain cell shape, and facilitate communication with the external environment, making it crucial for the cell's survival and function.

questions.subject: General Ability

questions.solution: A compound microscope typically consists of several parts including a mirror or light source (to illuminate the specimen), a stage (where the specimen is placed), clips (to hold the specimen slide in place), objective lenses (to magnify the specimen), an eyepiece or ocular lens (through which the observer views the specimen), and focusing knobs (to bring the specimen into sharp focus). Storage and regulated release of bile

questions.solution: The pancreas secretes enzymes such as lipase (to digest fats), amylase (to digest carbohydrates), and protease (to digest proteins) into the small intestine. Consider the following statements:

2. Chromatin organises itself into rod-shaped chromosomes before cell division.
3. Both prokaryotes and eukaryotes have the same process for cell division.

questions.solution:
Escape velocity is given by,
$\begin{array}{rlrl}
\Rightarrow & v & =\sqrt{2 g \mathrm{R}} \\

options: They need a medium to travel

questions.solution: Sound waves in fluids (liquids and gases) are longitudinal waves, not transverse. This means the vibrations occur in the same direction as the wave's propagation. Sound waves do transport energy and require a medium to travel because they propagate through the vibration of particles in the medium. The speed of sound generally increases in liquids compared to gases because liquids are denser and transmit sound more effectively.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Paragraph: The grouping or assemblage of plants, animals and microbes we observe when we study a natural forest, a grassland, a pond, a coral reef or some other undisturbed area, is referred to as the area's biota or biotic community. The plant portion of the biotic community includes all vegetation, from large trees down through to microscopic algae. Likewise, the animal portion includes everything from large mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians through to earthworms, tiny insects and mites. Microbes encompass a large array of microscopic bacteria, fungi and protozoans. Thus, the biotic community comprises a plant community, an animal community and a microbial community. The particular kind of biotic community found in a given area is, in large part, determined by abiotic factors such as the amount of water or moisture present, the temperature, the salinity, or the type of soil in the areThese abiotic factors both support and limit the particular community. For example, a relative lack of available moisture prevents the growth of most species of plants, but supports certain species, such as cacti; these kinds of areas are deserts. Land with plenty of available moisture and a suitable temperature supports forests. The presence of water is the major factor that sustains aquatic communities. The first step in investigating a biotic community may be simply to catalogue all the species present. Species are the different kinds of plants, animals and microbes in the community. A given species includes all those individuals which have a strong similarity in appearance to one another and which are distinct in appearance from other such groups. Each species in a biotic community is represented by a certain population - that is, by a certain number of individuals that make up the interbreeding, reproducing group.
Question: Species are defined on the basis of:
questions.solution: Species are defined as groups of individuals that are similar in appearance and distinct from other groups. This definition includes both similarities within the species and differences that distinguish one species from another.

For larger amplitude the restoring force is no longer directly proportional to displacement, Consequently the time period slightly dependent on the amplitude.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Water gas is a mixture of:
questions.solution:
Water gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide $(\mathrm{CO})$ and hydrogen $\left(\mathrm{H}_2\right)$, typically produced through a process known as gasification. In this process, steam $\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right.$ ) is passed over red-hot coke (a form of carbon), which results in the following endothermic reaction:
$\mathrm{C}(\text { coke })+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \text { (steam) } \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}+\mathrm{H}_2$
This reaction occurs at high temperatures and requires continuous heating to maintain the reaction. The resulting water gas, composed of CO and $\mathrm{H}_2$, can be used as a fuel or as an intermediate in the production of other chemicals. It is an important industrial process for generating a synthesis gas that can be used in various applications, including the synthesis of methanol and hydrocarbons via the Fischer-Tropsch process.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one among the following compounds has a sweet and fruity smell?
questions.solution: Ethyl acetate, known for its sweet and fruity smell, is commonly used in perfumes and flavorings. This ester is responsible for the pleasant aromas found in many fruits and is often utilized in the food and beverage industry to enhance flavors. Unlike ethyl alcohol, which has an alcoholic smell, and acetic acid, which has a sharp vinegar-like odor, ethyl acetate provides a distinctly sweet fragrance that is easily recognizable.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: What is the coordination number of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$and $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ ions in NaCl lattice?
questions.solution: In the NaCl (sodium chloride) crystal lattice, each sodium ion $\left(\mathrm{Na}^{+}\right)$is surrounded by 6 chloride ions ( $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$), and each chloride ion is surrounded by 6 sodium ions. This arrangement is known as a face-centered cubic (FCC) structure, where each ion is in contact with 6 nearest neighbours in all directions. This high coordination number of 6 ensures strong electrostatic interactions between ions, contributing to the stability of the crystal lattice and the characteristic properties of NaCl .

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one among the following is known as Milk of Magnesia?
questions.solution: Milk of Magnesia refers to a suspension of magnesium hydroxide in water, known for its medicinal use as an antacid and laxative. When ingested, it neutralizes stomach acid and provides relief from indigestion and heartburn due to its alkaline nature. It also acts as a mild laxative by drawing water into the intestines, thereby promoting bowel movements.

questions.solution: When soap is mixed with water, it forms a lyotropic liquid crystal. Lyotropic liquid crystals are formed by amphiphilic molecules (such as soap molecules) in solution. These molecules have both hydrophilic (water-attracting) and hydrophobic (waterrepelling) parts. In the presence of water, soap molecules self-organize into structures where the hydrophobic parts cluster together and the hydrophilic parts interact with water molecules.

questions.solution: Litmus, a natural dye used as an acid-base indicator, is derived from lichens. Lichens are symbiotic organisms composed of a fungus (usually an ascomycete) and an algae or cyanobacterium. Litmus is extracted from certain species of lichens and changes color depending on whether it is exposed to an acidic or basic environment.

Consider the two statements given below:
Statement-1: Infrared waves are also called heat waves.
Statement-2: Water molecules readily absorb infrarewaves.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
options: Both the statements are individually true and Statement-2 is the correct explanation of Statement-1.
Both the statements are individually true, but Statement-2 is not the correct explanation of Statement-1.
Statement-1 is true, but Statement-2 is false.
Statement-2 is true, but Statement-1 is false.
questions.solution: Infrared waves, also known as heat waves, are a type of electromagnetic radiation emitted by objects due to their temperature. Water molecules effectively absorb infrared waves, primarily through their vibrational modes, which results in the molecules gaining energy and contributing to heat. While it's accurate to call infrared waves "heat waves" due to their heating effect when absorbed by substances, this terminology doesn't solely stem from water's absorption behaviour. Therefore, both statements are individually correct. However, the absorption by water doesn't directly explain why infrared waves are termed heat waves in general usage.

questions.q: Bacterial DNA is referred to as naked because it is not associated with:
questions.solution: In bacteria, the DNA is not complexed with histone proteins or other structural proteins as in eukaryotic cells. Instead, bacterial DNA is typically a circular molecule that exists in a region of the cell called the nucleoid. This lack of histones or other associated proteins is why bacterial DNA is considered "naked".

questions.q: Human body works in the pH range of:
questions.solution: The human body maintains a tightly regulated pH range to ensure proper physiological function. This range is typically between 7.0 and 7.8 . The optimal pH for most body fluids, particularly blood, is around 7.4 , which is slightly alkaline. Enzyme activity, oxygen transport, and metabolic processes are all dependent on maintaining this pH range. Deviations from this range can lead to serious health issues, as enzymes and other biochemical processes may not function correctly if the pH is too acidic or too alkaline.

questions.q: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be two complex numbers such that $\left|\frac{z_1+z_2}{z_1-z_2}\right|=1$, then what is $\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right)+1$ equal to?
questions.solution:
Let $z_1=x_1+i y_1$ and $z_2=x_2+i y_2$
Now, $\quad\left|\frac{z_1+z_2}{z_1-z_2}\right|=1\begin{aligned}

& +\left(y_1-y_2\right)^2 \\
& \Rightarrow x_1^2+x_2^2+2 x_1 x_2+y_1^2+y_2^2+2 y_1 y_2 \\
& =x_1^2+x_2^2-2 x_1 x_2+y_1^2 \\
& +y_2^2-2 y_1 y_2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x_1 x_2+y_1 y_2=0 \\
& \frac{z_1}{z_2}=\frac{x_1+i y_1}{x_2+i y_2} \times \frac{x_2-i y_2}{x_2-i y_2} \\
& =\frac{\left(x_1 x_2+y_1 y_2\right)+i\left(y_1 x_2-x_1 y_2\right)}{x_2^2+y_2^2} \\
& =0+\frac{i\left(y_1 x_2-x_1 y_2\right)}{x_2^2+y_2^2}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right)=0 \\ & \therefore \quad \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right)+1=1 .\end{aligned}$

Let $3 f(x)+f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)=\frac{1}{x}+1$
What is $8 \int_1^2 f(x) d x$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} 8 \int_1^2 f(x) d x & =8 \int_1^2\left(\frac{3}{8 x}-\frac{x}{8}+\frac{1}{4}\right) d x \\ & =\int_1^2\left(\frac{3}{x}-x+2\right) d x \\ & =\left[3 \ln x-\frac{x^2}{2}+2 x\right]_1^2 \\ & =\left(3 \ln 2-\frac{4}{2}+4\right)-\left(3 \ln 1-\frac{1}{2}+2\right) \\ & =3 \ln 2+2-\frac{3}{2}=\frac{1}{2}+3 \ln 2 \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \ln e+\ln 2^3=\ln \sqrt{e}+\ln 8 \\ & =\ln (8 \sqrt{e})\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What are the order and degree respectively of the differential equation $\left\{2-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right\}^{0.6}=\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}$ ?
questions.solution:
$\left\{2-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right\}^{0.6}=\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}$
Removing decimal power/fraction power both sides
$\left\{2-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right\}^{3 / 5}=\left(\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^5$
Raise power of 5 both sides
$\begin{aligned}
& \left\{2-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right\}^{\frac{3}{5} \times 5}=\left(\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^5 \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \left\{2-\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2\right\}^3=\left(\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^5
\end{aligned}$
Hence,
$\begin{aligned}
\text { Order } & =2 \\
\text { Power } & =5
\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Let $\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c$
What is the value of $\beta$ ?
questions.solution:
Given,
$\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\alpha(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\beta(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c\qquad ....(i)$
Let, $\quad \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}\begin{aligned}
& =\int \frac{(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1}) d x}{(\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1})(\sqrt{x+1}+\sqrt{x-1})} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{(x+1)} d x+\frac{1}{2} \int \sqrt{x-1} d x \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+\frac{\frac{1}{2}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt{x-1}}=\frac{1}{3}(x+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c \ldots(ii)
\end{aligned}$
From (i) and (ii) we get
$\beta=\frac{1}{3}$

questions.q:
Given that $\int \frac{3 \cos x+4 \sin x}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x=\frac{\alpha x}{29}+\frac{\beta}{29} \ln |2 \cos x+5 \sin x|+c$
What is the value of $\beta$ ?
questions.solution:
Let,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}=\int \frac{3 \cos x+4 \sin x}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
& 3 \cos x+4 \sin x=\mathrm{A}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x) \\
& +\mathrm{B}\left[\frac{d}{d x}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)\right] \\
& 3 \cos x+4 \sin x=\mathrm{A}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x) \\
& +\mathrm{B}(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)
\end{aligned}$
Comparing co-efficient of $\sin x$ and $\cos x\begin{aligned}
& 3=2 A+5 B \qquad ....(i)\\
& 4=5 A-2 B \qquad ....(ii)
\end{aligned}$
Solving (i) and (ii) then we get,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{A}=\frac{26}{29}, \mathrm{~B}=\frac{7}{29} \\
& \mathrm{I}=\frac{\int \frac{26}{29}(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)+\frac{7}{29}(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
&=\int \frac{26}{29} d x+\frac{7}{29} \int \frac{(-2 \sin x+5 \cos x)}{2 \cos x+5 \sin x} d x \\
&=\frac{26}{29} x+\frac{7}{29} \text { In }(2 \cos x+5 \sin x)+c \\
& \alpha=26, \beta=7[\text { [on comparing] }
\end{aligned}\beta=7$

& =\frac{(a+c)}{(a-c)}\left[-\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{c}\right] \\

& =\frac{2}{b}=\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{b}=\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{c}\right)
\end{aligned}$
Hence, only statement (1) and (2) are correct. Statement (3) is not correct.

questions.q: If $(1,-1,2)$ and $(2,1,-1)$ are the end points of a diameter of a sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2+2 u x+2 v y+2 w z-1=0$, then what is $u+v+w$ equal to?
questions.solution:
The general equation $x^2+y^2+z^2+2 u x+2 v y+2 w z+d=0$ represents a sphere with centre $(-u,-v,-w)$ and radius $r=\sqrt{u^2+v^2+w^2-d}$ If $B$ is the mid point of the line segment $A C$ where $\mathrm{A}=\left(x_1, y_1, z_1\right)$ and $\mathrm{C}=\left(x_2, y_2, z_2\right)$ then. $\mathrm{B}=\left(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1+y_2}{2}, \frac{z_1+z_2}{2}\right)$ Given, equation of sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2+2 u x+2 v y+2 w z-1=0$ with AB as its diameter and $\mathrm{A}=(1,-1,2)$ and $\mathrm{B}=(2,1,-1)$
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{C} & =\left(\frac{1+2}{2}, \frac{1-1}{2}, \frac{-1+2}{2}\right) \\ & =\left(\frac{3}{2}, 0, \frac{1}{2}\right) \end{aligned}$ We know that centre of the sphere is given by $(-u,-v,-w)$ Comparing, then we get, $\left(\frac{3}{2}, 0, \frac{1}{2}\right)=(-u,-v,-w)\begin{aligned} u & =-\frac{3}{2}, v=0, w=-\frac{1}{2} \\ \therefore u+v+w & =-\frac{3}{2}+0-\frac{1}{2}=-\frac{4}{2}=-2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\langle l, m, n \gt $ are the direction cosines of a normal to the plane $2 x-3 y+6 z+4=0$, then what is the value of $49\left(7 l^2+m^2-n^2\right)$ ?
questions.solution:
The plane equation is $a x+b y+c z=d$
Given the plane equation is $2 x-3 y+6 z+4=0\Rightarrow \quad 2 x-3 y+6 z=-4$
Comparing then we get,
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{a}=2, b & =-3, c=6, d=-4 \\
\therefore \quad \sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2} & =\sqrt{(2)^2+(-3)^2+(6)^2} \\
& =\sqrt{4+9+36}=\sqrt{49}=7
\end{aligned}$
Direction cosines of normal to the plane
$\begin{aligned}
l & =\frac{a}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}=\frac{2}{7} \\
m & =\frac{b}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}=-\frac{3}{7} \\
n & =\frac{c}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}=\frac{6}{7} \\
 \lt l, m, n \gt  & =\left\langle\frac{2}{7},-\frac{3}{7}, \frac{6}{7}\right\rangle \\
\therefore \quad 49\left(7 l^2+m^2-n^2\right) & =49\left[7\left(\frac{2}{7}\right)^2+\left(-\frac{3}{7}\right)^2-\left(\frac{6}{7}\right)^2\right] \\
& =49\left[\frac{28}{49}+\frac{9}{49}-\frac{36}{49}\right] \\
& =49\left[\frac{1}{49}\right]=1
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $p$ is the perpendicular distance from origin to the plane passing through $(1,0,0),(0,1,0)$ and $(0,0,1)$, then what is $3 p^2$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$\because$ Plane passing through $(1,0,0),(0,1,0)$ and $(0,0,1)\vec{a}=\hat{i}, \vec{b}=\hat{j}, \vec{c}=\hat{k}$
Let,
$\hat{r}=x \hat{i}+y \hat{j}+z \hat{k}\begin{aligned}
& (\vec{r}-\vec{a}) \cdot[(\vec{b}-\vec{a}) \times(\vec{c}-\vec{a})]=0 \\
& \begin{aligned}
\vec{b}-\vec{a} & =\hat{j}-\hat{i} \text { and } \vec{c}-\vec{a}=\hat{k}-\hat{i} \\
\therefore \quad(\vec{b}-\vec{a}) \times(\vec{c}-\vec{a}) & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\
-1 & 1 & 0 \\
-1 & 0 & 1
\end{array}\right|=\hat{i} \hat{j} \hat{k} \\
\therefore \quad(\vec{r}-\vec{a}) & =(x \hat{i}+y \hat{j}+z \hat{k})-(\hat{i}) \\
& =(x-1) \hat{i}+y \hat{j}+z \hat{k}
\end{aligned}
\end{aligned}$
We have,
$\begin{aligned}
{[(x-1) \hat{i}+y \hat{j}+z \hat{k}] \cdot(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) } & =0 \\
\quad & (x-1)+y+z=0
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Equating of plane $x+y+z-1=0\perp$ distance from origin to the plane
$=\frac{|-1|}{\sqrt{(1)^2+(1)^2+(1)^2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \text { unit }\begin{aligned} \text { Here, } & & p & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow p^2=\frac{1}{3} \\ & \therefore & 3 p^2 & =1\end{aligned}$

Direction ratios of the line from the point (1, -1, 2) to the given plane is $\langle 3,2,2\rangle\therefore \quad \frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y+1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{2}=\lambda$ Co-ordinates any points on the line PQ are $\begin{aligned} & x=3 \lambda+1, y=2 \lambda-1, z=2 \lambda+2 \\ & x+2 y+3 z=18 \\ & \therefore \quad 3 \lambda+1+4 \lambda-2+6 \lambda+6=18 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 13 \lambda+5=18 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 13 \lambda=13 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \lambda \end{aligned}$ Hence, the co-ordinates of Q are $(3+1,2-1,2+2)=(4,1,4)$

& \begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad l^2+m^2-n^2 & =\frac{64}{101}+\frac{1}{101}-\frac{36}{101} \\

questions.q: If a vector of magnitude 2 units makes an angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ with $2 \hat{i}, \frac{\pi}{4}$ with $3 \hat{j}$ and an acute angle $\theta$ with $4 \hat{k}$, then what are the components of the vector?
questions.solution:
Let, $\vec{a}$ have $\left(a_1, a_2, a_3\right)$ components
$\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & a_1 \hat{i}+a_2 \hat{j}+a_3 \hat{k} \\
\because & |\vec{a}|=2
\end{array}
Also, It is given that $\vec{a}$ make angle with $\frac{\pi}{3}$ with $2 \hat{i}$, $\frac{\pi}{4}$ with $3 \hat{j}$ and an acute angle $\theta$ with $4 \hat{k}$ Then we have,
$\begin{aligned}
\vec{a} \cdot 2 \hat{i} & =|\vec{a}||2 \hat{i}| \cos \frac{\pi}{3} \\
\left(a_1 \hat{i}+a_2 \hat{j}+a_3 \hat{k}\right) \cdot 2 \hat{i} & =2.2 \times \frac{1}{2} \\
2 a_1 & =2 \Rightarrow a_1=1 \\
\therefore \quad \vec{a} \cdot 3 \hat{j} & =|\vec{a}||3 \hat{j}| \cos \frac{\pi}{4}
\end{aligned}$
and
$3 a_2=2 \times 3 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow a_2=\sqrt{2}\begin{aligned}
\vec{a} \cdot 4 \hat{k} & =|\vec{a}||4 \hat{k}| \cos \theta \\
4 a_3 & =2 \times 4 \cos \theta
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \cos \theta=\frac{a_3}{2}$
Now, $\quad|\vec{a}|=2\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & \sqrt{a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2}=2 \\
\Rightarrow & a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2=4
\end{array}
Put, $a_1=1$ and $a_2=\sqrt{2}(1)^2+(\sqrt{2})^2+a_3^2=4 \Rightarrow a_3^2= \pm 1$
When,
$a_3=-1$
then,
$\cos \theta=-\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow \quad \theta=\frac{2 \pi}{3} \gt \frac{\pi}{2}$ (contradict)
$\because \theta$ is acute angle with $4 \hat{k}\therefore \quad a_3=1$
Hence, the components of $\vec{a}=(1, \sqrt{2}, 1)$.

questions.q: If $f(\theta)=\frac{1}{1+\tan \theta}$ and $\alpha+\beta=\frac{5 \pi}{4}$, then what is the value of $f(\alpha) f(\beta)$ ?
questions.solution: $\alpha+\beta=\frac{5 \pi}{4}\begin{aligned} & \tan (\alpha+\beta)=\tan 5 \frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\tan \alpha+\tan \beta}{1-\tan \alpha \times \tan \beta}=\tan \left(\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\tan \frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\tan \alpha+\tan \beta}{1-\tan \alpha \times \tan \beta}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \tan \alpha+\tan \beta=1-\tan \alpha \times \tan \beta \\ & \Rightarrow \tan \alpha+\tan \beta+\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta=1 \\ & \because f(\theta)=\frac{1}{1+\tan \theta} \\ & f(\alpha) \cdot f(\beta)=\frac{1}{1+\tan \alpha+\tan \beta+\tan \alpha \cdot \tan \beta}=\frac{1}{1+1}=\frac{1}{2} .\end{aligned}$

questions.q: What is the value of $\tan 65^{\circ}+2 \tan 45^{\circ}-2 \tan40^{\circ}-\tan 25^{\circ} ?$

questions.q: What is $\frac{\sqrt{3} \cos 10^{\circ}-\sin 10^{\circ}}{\sin 25^{\circ} \cos 25^{\circ}}$ equal to?

questions.q: What is the value of $\sin 10^{\circ} \cdot \sin 50^{\circ}+\sin 50^{\circ}$. $\sin 250^{\circ}+\sin 250^{\circ} \cdot \sin 10^{\circ}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sin 10^{\circ} \cdot \sin 50^{\circ}+ \sin 50^{\circ} \cdot \sin 250^{\circ} \\ &+\sin 250^{\circ} \cdot \sin 10^{\circ}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\cos 40^{\circ}-\cos 60^{\circ}+\cos 200^{\circ}\right. \\ & \quad-\cos 300^{\circ}+\cos 240^{\circ}-\cos 260^{\circ} \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\begin{array}{l}\cos 40^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2}+\cos (180+20)^{\circ}-\cos (360-60)^{\circ} \\ +\cos (180+60)^{\circ}-\cos (180+80)^{\circ}\end{array}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 40^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2}-\cos 20^{\circ}-\cos 60^{\circ}-\cos 60^{\circ}+\cos 80^{\circ}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 40^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}+\cos 80^{\circ}-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 40^{\circ}+\cos 80^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{3}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[2 \cos \left(\frac{80+40}{2}\right) \times \cos \left(\frac{80-40}{2}\right)-\cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{3}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[2 \cos 60^{\circ} \cdot \cos 20^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{3}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[2 \times \frac{1}{2} \cdot \cos 20^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{3}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\cos 20^{\circ}-\cos 20^{\circ}-\frac{3}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[-\frac{3}{2}\right]=-\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are two vectors of magnitude 4 inclined at an angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$, then what is the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{a}-\vec{b}$ ?
questions.solution:
The angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{a}-\vec{b}$ is given by
$\cos \theta=\frac{\vec{a} \cdot(\vec{a}-\vec{b})}{|\vec{a}||\vec{a}-\vec{b}|}$
Now, $\quad \vec{a} \cdot(\vec{a}-\vec{b})=\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a}-\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\therefore \quad \vec{a} \cdot \vec{a}=|\vec{a}|^2$
Given that magnitude of $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is 4
$\begin{aligned}
|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}| & =4 \\
|\vec{a}|^2 & =4^2=16
\end{aligned}$
and$\qquad \vec{a} \vec{b}=|\vec{a} \| \vec{b}| \cos \frac{\pi}{3}=4 \cdot 4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}=8\begin{aligned}
|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|^2 & =|\vec{a}|^2+|\vec{b}|^2-\vec{a} \vec{b}-\vec{b} \vec{a} \\
& =16+16-8-8=16 \\
\cos \theta & =\frac{16-8}{4 \sqrt{16}}=\frac{8}{4 \cdot 4}=\frac{1}{2}=\cos \frac{\pi}{3}
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For any vector $\vec{r}$, what is $(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{i})(\vec{r} \times \hat{i})+(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{j})(\vec{r} \times \hat{j})+(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{k})(\vec{r} \times \hat{k})$ equal to?
questions.solution:
$(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{i})(\vec{r} \times \hat{i})+(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{j})(\vec{r} \times \hat{j})+(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{k})(\vec{r} \times \hat{k})$ ...(i)
We have,
$\begin{aligned} \vec{r} & =a \hat{i}+b \hat{j}+c \hat{k} \\ (\vec{r} \hat{i}) & =(a \hat{i}+b \hat{j}+c \hat{k}) \cdot \hat{i}=a \\ (\vec{r} \cdot \hat{j}) & =b \\ (\vec{r} \cdot \hat{k}) & =c\end{aligned}$
and $\qquad \vec{r} \times \hat{i}=\left|\begin{array}{lll}
\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\
a & b & c \\
1 & 0 & 0
\end{array}\right|=-\hat{j}(-c)-b \hat{k}=c \hat{j}-b \hat{k}$
Similarly, $\quad \vec{r} \times \hat{j}=-c \hat{i}+a \hat{k}$
and$\vec{r} \hat{k}=b \hat{i}-a \hat{j}$
Putting these values in (i) we get
$\begin{aligned}
& a(\hat{j}-b \hat{k})+b(-c \hat{i}+a \hat{k})+c(b \hat{i}-a \hat{j}) \\
&=a c \hat{j}-a b \hat{k}-b c \hat{i}+a b \hat{k}+b c \hat{i}-a c \hat{j}=0
\end{aligned}$
